messages:
maya: Kicking off the pacific3 region soak + autoscale tuning now. Plan: 12h soak, 4 phases (warmup, steady, spike, recovery). Handing off to @kevin after validation. Watch GPU pool scale and networking egress limits.
kevin: Ack. Can you paste the bootstrap commands and the thresholds we agreed?
maya: Bootstrap snippets below — used to create node pools and attach GPU quota. Note these are simplified: 
```bash
rcli region create --name pacific3 --cloud gcp --zone us-west3-a 
  --gpu-pool "gpu-a100-8" --node-count 4 --preemptible=false
rcli quota request --region pacific3 --gpu 32
kubectl apply -f pacific3/network-policies.yaml
```
Also validating IAM roles + KMS access before any traffic.
kevin: Good. For autoscaler we set HPA target 60% GPU utilization + custom metric for request_queue_length < 200. If GPU preempts, fallback to burst nodes (smaller cheaper GPUs) then to next region.
oliver: Couple notes from SRE perspective:
- Use KEDA for queue-driven scale on async workloads, native HPA for sync.
- Set pod disruption budgets wide enough to allow rolling priming: pdb minAvailable: 70%.
- Node autoscaler: scale-down-delay 15m, scale-up-cooldown 90s.
- Monitor these: node_count, pod_pending, gpu_util, pci_errors, network_drops.
maya: Starting Phase 1 (warmup) at t+0: a gentle 30% of expected production qps. Running k6 script in background:
```bash
k6 run --vus 50 --duration 15m ./scripts/pacific3-warmup.js
```
devops: For load phases:
- Phase 2 steady: 60% for 3h
- Phase 3 spike: ramp to 150% for 20m (simulate burst without reserved capacity)
- Phase 4 recovery: drop to 10% then step up to baseline
Use both inference and control-plane ops concurrently to validate API gateway and control-plane throttles.
kevin: Noted. Observability dash URLs: 
- GPU fleet: https://console.redwood/grafana/d/gpu-fleet/pacific3
- Autoscale: https://console.redwood/grafana/d/autoscale/pacific3
Alerts to watch (pager oncall if >5m): node_not_ready_count > 3; pod_pending > 10 for >10m; sustained_gpu_util > 85% for 10m.
sre-bot: Alert: 1801234572 node-drain event detected: "taint:preemptible=true" on node gpu-a100-8-2. Docs: https://internal/status/1801234572
kevin: Saw that — one preemptible fell out of pool. That's expected for preemptible configurations. For this run we keep preemptible=false for the primary pool, but we will test preemptible as burst in next window.
maya: Phase 3 starting in 30m. Reminder: during spike we'll temporarily relax scale-down to 5m to avoid churning when load drops. Also we'll flip feature flag to degrade to smaller model if latency > 750ms for 3m.
devops: Load generator command for spike (k6) and sample headers:
```bash
k6 run --vus 300 --duration 20m --out influxdb=http://metrics:8086 ./scripts/pacific3-spike.js
# headers: x-deployment: pacific3-soak x-traffic-source: soak-suite
```
oliver: Cost note — spike-to-burst will spin up on-demand GPUs and then down to preemptible for recovery. Estimate: extra ~USD 2.8k for the 12h run if we allow 1.5x peak. Recommend we cap spike to 120% if finance flags it.
kevin: Finance OK'd up to 150% for this run but asked for a cost-runbook: if projected cost >$3k, abort spike and move to simulated load (no real GPU spin).
maya: We'll export a cost estimate at t+1h and post to the ticket. Also creating the handoff checklist for post-soak:
- confirm all alerts resolved
- collect failing pods + stack traces (if any)
- snapshot dashboards and attach to ticket
- create rollout plan for Dedicated capacity if needed
kevin: After soak I will open a follow-up note with tuned autoscaler params: target_util, cooldowns, and any model fallback rules.
maya: Quick sanity logs pulled:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep pacific3
NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS
inference-xyz-1                        1/1     Running   0
inference-xyz-2                        1/1     Running   0
```
All good for now. Starting phase 2 in 10m. Ping me here for any immediate pager events. :thumbsup:
